purpose: Additional held-out pacing/disclosure cases, not a training batch. Manual review prompts never enter model inputs.

cases.title: Buyer: simple unexpected call, limited invitation

payload.context: Unexpected first call. Buyer has only heard a request for a moment.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi Rachel, Omri at Salesforce. Have you got a moment?

cases.manual_review: Does the buyer respond to the attention request without unloading pains, causes, unknown metrics and a stakeholder? Variation is fine; no fact-count threshold or required phrase.

cases.title: Buyer: scheduled conversation invites detail

payload.context: Buyer has agreed to a scheduled discovery conversation and is invited to explain what they know.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi Omri. I’ve set aside some time for this.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thanks for making the time. Could you walk me through the delivery investigation issue your managers raised and what you know about it?

cases.manual_review: Can a willing buyer offer useful connected detail without becoming artificially terse? Does uncertainty remain proportionate to actual knowledge? This is a counterexample to a universal brevity rule.

cases.title: Stakeholder knowledge boundary, no invitation

payload.context: Unexpected expansion call to a logistics leader. No concrete consequential problem or project has been established.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Does the dispatch handoff ever create extra work?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Occasionally, I suppose. Our planning lead knows the details better than I do.

cases.manual_review: Does the coach distinguish a knowledge boundary from permission for a meeting? Could a useful statement, modest clarification or respectful exit fit better? No mandatory next move.

cases.title: Buyer explicitly invites stakeholder involvement

payload.context: Unscheduled call has become engaged. Buyer supplies a consequential problem and an explicit invitation.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: It may be worth understanding the dispatch handoff.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It is. Missed handoffs are delaying priority deliveries every week. I want you to look at this with Dana, our planning lead. Could the three of us talk Thursday?

cases.manual_review: Can the coach accept and clarify useful logistics without forcing more qualification? Do not manufacture a delay merely to avoid early meetings.

cases.title: Opening: executive interruption, no diagnosis requested

payload.context: A first unexpected expansion call. No prior substantive dialogue or confirmed buyer pain.

cases.manual_review: Does the new opener establish an honest reason to engage without asking the executive to diagnose a broad business metric? Before-pacing column must show the actual old UI opener, not a guessed old model answer.

cases.title: Clear early redirect without full discovery

payload.context: Cold outbound to a person who explicitly redirects the seller. No agreement or endorsement beyond the stated permission.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I was calling about support operations.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That belongs to Lena now. Please contact her directly—you can say I pointed you to her. I’m not involved in that anymore.

cases.manual_review: Can the coach accept the redirect and close without demanding a problem statement or automatically proposing a joint meeting? Referral permission is not a confirmed appointment.
